items.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Lina cuts a 5 cm square off one end. What is the perimeter of the rectangle that is left?

figure.alt: A rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. A square 5 cm by 5 cm is cut off one end.

options.why: 10 cm is only two of the sides.
The piece left is 3 cm long, not 4 cm.
26 cm is the perimeter of the whole rectangle before the cut.

hints: Find the size of the piece that is left.
The piece left is 8 - 5 cm long and still 5 cm wide.
The piece is 3 cm by 5 cm. Add its four sides.
items.explanation: The piece left is 3 cm by 5 cm. Its perimeter is 3 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 16 cm.

items.prompt: A square with sides of 8 cm is cut into 4 equal strips. The cuts are parallel to one side. What is the perimeter of one strip?

figure.alt: A square with sides of 8 cm, cut into 4 equal strips by 3 straight cuts.

options.why: 8 cm is only one long side.
Count all four sides of the strip: 8 + 2 + 8 + 2.
Each strip is 2 cm wide, not 1 cm.
32 cm is the perimeter of the whole square.

hints: Find how wide each strip is.
The 8 cm side is shared by 4 strips.
Each strip is 8 cm long and 8 ÷ 4 cm wide.
items.explanation: Each strip is 8 cm long and 2 cm wide. Its perimeter is 8 + 2 + 8 + 2 = 20 cm.

items.prompt: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube is painted on the outside. Then it is cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 painted faces?

figure.alt: A big cube made of 27 small cubes, 3 along each edge. The outside of the big cube is painted.

options.why: 1 cube in the very centre has no paint at all.
6 small cubes sit in the middle of the faces. They have only 1 painted face.
The 8 corner cubes have 3 painted faces, not 2.
9 is the number of small cubes on one face.

hints: Think about where a small cube sits: corner, edge, face or centre.
Corner cubes have 3 painted faces. Cubes in the middle of a face have 1.
Cubes with exactly 2 painted faces sit in the middle of an edge.
items.explanation: Cubes with exactly 2 painted faces are on the edges but not at the corners. Each of the 12 edges has 1 such cube, so there are 12.

solution.say: Middle of each edge: 2 painted faces.
Middle of each face: 1 painted face.
Centre: no paint. Check the total.

items.prompt: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at exactly 4 o'clock?

figure.alt: A clock showing 4 o'clock. The hour hand points to 4 and the minute hand points to 12.

options.why: The hands are 4 hour marks apart, and each mark is 30°.
Each hour mark is 30°, so 4 marks make 120°.

hints: A full turn is 360°, and the clock face has 12 hour marks.
From one hour mark to the next is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
At 4 o'clock the hands are 4 hour marks apart.
items.explanation: Each hour mark is 30°. At 4 o'clock the hands are 4 marks apart, so the angle is 4 × 30° = 120°.

solution.say: Marks between the hands at 4 o'clock.

items.prompt: A staircase shape is made of squares with sides of 1 cm. The rows have 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 squares, lined up on the left. What is its perimeter?

figure.alt: A staircase of 1 cm squares: the top row has 1 square, then 2, 3 and 4, and the bottom row has 5 squares, all lined up on the left.

hints: Trace the outline and count the 1 cm edges.
The steps on the right can be pushed out to make straight lines.
The outline is as long as the outline of a 5 cm by 5 cm square.
items.explanation: The flat and upright parts of the steps add up to 5 cm across and 5 cm up. So the outline is as long as the outline of a 5 cm square: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 cm.

solution.say: The left side and the bottom are straight.
The steps go across 5 cm in total and up 5 cm in total.

items.prompt: A floor is 3 m long and 2 m wide. It is covered with square tiles with sides of 50 cm. How many tiles are needed?

figure.alt: A rectangular floor 3 m long and 2 m wide.

options.why: 6 tiles would be enough only if each tile were 1 m wide.
Count again. Both sides need 2 tiles for every metre.
Check the width: 2 m needs 4 tiles, and 3 m needs 6 tiles.

hints: How many 50 cm tiles fit along 1 metre?
2 tiles fit along every metre.
Along 3 m fit 6 tiles. Along 2 m fit 4 tiles.
items.explanation: Two 50 cm tiles fit in each metre. The floor is 6 tiles long and 4 tiles wide, so it needs 6 × 4 = 24 tiles.

items.prompt: A big square is made of 9 small squares, 3 by 3. The perimeter of the big square is 36 cm. What is the area of one small square?

figure.alt: A big square made of 9 small squares in 3 rows of 3. The perimeter of the big square is 36 cm.

hints: Find the side of the big square first.
The big square has 4 equal sides that make 36 cm.
Each side of the big square is made of 3 small sides.
items.explanation: The big square's side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm, which is 3 small sides, so a small side is 3 cm. One small square has an area of 3 × 3 = 9 cm².

items.prompt: In a big triangle, two lines go from the top corner down to the bottom side. A third line crosses the triangle, parallel to the bottom side. How many triangles are there in the picture?

figure.alt: A big triangle. Two lines go from the top corner to the bottom side, making 3 thin triangles side by side. One more line crosses the whole triangle, parallel to the bottom side.

hints: Every triangle in this picture has the top corner as one of its corners.
Its bottom side lies either on the crossing line or on the bottom side of the big triangle.
Count the triangles with their bottom side on the crossing line first.
items.explanation: Every triangle uses the top corner and 2 of the 4 lines that come out of it, and those lines can be paired in 6 ways. Each pair is closed off either by the crossing line or by the bottom side, so there are 6 + 6 = 12 triangles.

solution.say: Lines from the top corner: the 2 sides of the big triangle and the 2 lines inside.
Each pair makes one triangle with the crossing line and one with the bottom side.

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is twice its width. What is its area?
hints: Call the width one part. Then the length is two parts.
Going all the way round uses 2 widths and 2 lengths, which is 6 parts.
6 parts make 30 cm, so one part is 30 ÷ 6 cm.
items.explanation: The perimeter is 6 widths, so the width is 30 ÷ 6 = 5 cm and the length is 10 cm. The area is 10 × 5 = 50 cm².

solution.say: Perimeter in parts: width 1 part, length 2 parts.

items.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is the distance around it, in cm?
hints: The distance around is the perimeter.
A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
items.explanation: The sides are 8, 5, 8 and 5 cm. The perimeter is 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.

items.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. How long is one side, in cm?
hints: A square has 4 equal sides.
Share the perimeter between the 4 sides.
items.explanation: The 4 sides are equal and they add up to 36 cm. One side is 36 / 4 = 9 cm.

solution.say: The 4 sides are equal and they add up to 36 cm.

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm. Its length is 8 cm. What is its width, in cm?
hints: The two lengths use some of the perimeter.
Share what is left between the two widths.
items.explanation: The two lengths are 8 + 8 = 16 cm. That leaves 24 - 16 = 8 cm for the two widths. One width is 8 / 2 = 4 cm.

solution.say: That leaves 24 - 16 = 8 cm for the two widths.

items.prompt: Each small square has sides of 1 cm. What is the distance around the shaded L shape, in cm?

figure.alt: An L shape of 5 shaded small squares: a column of 3 and a row of 3 sharing the bottom left square.

hints: Count the edges around the outside.
Go all the way round, starting at the top left.
Count each edge of 1 cm.
items.explanation: Going round the shape: down the left 3, along the bottom 3, up 1, along 2 to the left, up 2 and along 1 to the left. That is 3 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 12 cm.

solution.say: Going round the shape: down the left 3, along the bottom 3, up 1, along 2 to the left, up 2 and along 1 to the left.

items.prompt: Two squares with sides of 3 cm are joined side to side to make a rectangle. What is the distance around the rectangle, in cm?
hints: Draw the rectangle. How long and how wide is it?
It is 6 cm long and 3 cm wide.
Add all four sides.
items.explanation: The rectangle is 3 + 3 = 6 cm long and 3 cm wide. The distance around is 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 cm.

solution.say: The rectangle is 3 + 3 = 6 cm long and 3 cm wide.

items.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
hints: A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
Each corner has one line going to the middle of the opposite side.
Count the corners.
items.explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 corners. There is a line of symmetry from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. So there are 3 lines.

solution.say: There is a line of symmetry from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.

items.prompt: A cube has edges of 3 cm. What is the total length of all its edges, in cm?

figure.alt: A cube, a solid with 6 square faces.

hints: A cube has 12 edges.
All the edges are 3 cm long.
items.explanation: A cube has 12 edges and each is 3 cm long. The total is 12 x 3 = 36 cm.

solution.say: A cube has 12 edges and each is 3 cm long.

items.prompt: A big cube is made of 4 by 4 by 4 small cubes. It is painted red all over and then taken apart. How many small cubes have red paint on exactly 2 faces?
hints: A cube with exactly 2 painted faces sits on an edge, but not at a corner.
The big cube has 12 edges.
Each edge has 4 cubes. 2 of them are corners.
items.explanation: On each of the 12 edges, 4 small cubes are in a row. The 2 at the ends are corners. The 2 in the middle have exactly 2 painted faces. So there are 12 x 2 = 24 cubes.

solution.say: On each of the 12 edges, 4 small cubes are in a row.
The 2 at the ends are corners.
The 2 in the middle have exactly 2 painted faces.

items.prompt: A big cube is made of 4 by 4 by 4 small cubes. It is painted red all over and then taken apart. How many small cubes have no red paint?
hints: Cubes with no paint are inside the big cube.
Take away the outside layer on every side.
What size cube is left in the middle?
items.explanation: Take away the outside layer on every side. A cube of 2 by 2 by 2 is left inside. That is 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cubes with no paint.

solution.say: Take away the outside layer on every side.
A cube of 2 by 2 by 2 is left inside.
That is 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cubes with no paint.

items.prompt: A square with sides of 4 cm is cut into 4 equal small squares. What is the distance around one small square, in cm?
hints: Find the side of a small square.
The big square is 4 cm wide and is cut into 2 small squares across.
Each small square has sides of 2 cm.
items.explanation: The big square is cut into 2 by 2 small squares. Each small square has sides of 4 / 2 = 2 cm. The distance around is 4 x 2 = 8 cm.

solution.say: The big square is cut into 2 by 2 small squares.
Each small square has sides of 4 / 2 = 2 cm.
The distance around is 4 x 2 = 8 cm.

items.prompt: A big triangle has 3 lines drawn from its top corner to the bottom side. They split the bottom into 4 parts. How many triangles of any size are there?

figure.alt: A big triangle with 3 lines from the top corner to the bottom side. They split the bottom into 4 equal parts.

hints: Count the triangles by their bottom parts.
There are 4 small triangles. Count those made of 2 small ones.
There are 3 of those. Then count 3 together and 4 together.
items.explanation: The bottom has 4 parts. A triangle takes 1, 2, 3 or 4 parts side by side. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 triangles.

solution.say: A triangle takes 1, 2, 3 or 4 parts side by side.
